s1.syndrome_frame: Subacute neurological decline with mass effect and subsequent respiratory decompensation in an immunocompromised host
salient_findings: Ring-enhancing lesion in the right temporal lobe with mass effect
Elevated serum toxoplasma IgG and positive toxoplasma IgG and DNA-PCR for Toxoplasma gondii in CSF
New left upper lobe opacification with diffuse reticulonodular interstitial prominence on chest radiograph
key_facts: 1½-week history of headache and blurred vision
MRI showed a 2.7-cm ring-enhancing lesion in the right temporal lobe
Patient underwent craniotomy with biopsy and resection
Postoperative diagnosis of HIV infection with a CD4 count <20 cells/µL
HIV viral load of 191 000 copies/mL
Elevated serum toxoplasma IgG
CSF studies showed 48 cells/µL (97% lymphocytes) with positive toxoplasma IgG and DNA-PCR for Toxoplasma gondii
Histopathologic examination of the brain tissue revealed bradyzoites and tachyzoites
Patient was treated with trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole and started on antiretroviral therapy
Two weeks after discharge, patient returned with fever to 39.6 °C, generalized weakness, and a 1-day history of productive cough
Chest radiograph showed a new left upper lobe opacification with diffuse reticulonodular interstitial prominence

shortlist.label: Toxoplasmosis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has elevated serum toxoplasma IgG, CSF studies showed positive toxoplasma IgG and DNA-PCR for Toxoplasma gondii, and histopathologic examination of the brain tissue revealed bradyzoites and tachyzoites

shortlist.label: Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia
shortlist.why_kept: Patient is immunocompromised with a CD4 count <20 cells/µL and presented with respiratory symptoms and diffuse reticulonodular interstitial prominence on chest radiograph

shortlist.label: Cytomegalovirus pneumonia
shortlist.why_kept: Patient is immunocompromised and presented with fever, generalized weakness, and respiratory symptoms

shortlist.label: Invasive aspergillosis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient is immunocompromised and presented with fever, generalized weakness, and respiratory symptoms, and has a history of neurological decline with mass effect

shortlist.label: Primary central nervous system lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Patient presented with a 2.7-cm ring-enhancing lesion in the right temporal lobe and has a history of HIV infection

raw.rationale: The patient's initial presentation with a ring-enhancing lesion in the brain, elevated serum toxoplasma IgG, positive toxoplasma IgG and DNA-PCR for Toxoplasma gondii in CSF, and histopathologic examination showing bradyzoites and tachyzoites are all consistent with toxoplasmosis, particularly in the context of a severely immunocompromised state due to HIV infection with a very low CD4 count.

rejected.label: Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia
rejected.why: While the patient's immunocompromised state puts him at risk for Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia, the initial presentation and diagnostic findings are more specific for toxoplasmosis, and there is no direct evidence provided for Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia in the vignette.

rejected.label: Cytomegalovirus pneumonia
rejected.why: There is no specific evidence provided in the vignette that suggests cytomegalovirus pneumonia, such as positive CMV PCR in the blood or respiratory secretions, or characteristic histopathologic findings.

rejected.label: Invasive aspergillosis
rejected.why: The patient's presentation and the findings do not specifically suggest invasive aspergillosis, and the treatment and diagnostic workup described do not include evidence that would typically point towards this diagnosis, such as positive Aspergillus PCR or galactomannan antigen in the blood.

rejected.label: Primary central nervous system lymphoma
rejected.why: While this could be a consideration in an immunocompromised patient, the specific findings of toxoplasma IgG elevation, positive DNA-PCR for Toxoplasma gondii, and the presence of bradyzoites and tachyzoites in the brain tissue are more indicative of toxoplasmosis than lymphoma.
